key_terms.definition: The first stage of Jewish marriage, by which a woman becomes legally married to a man. Relations with another man are then adultery, and only a get or the husband's death can end the bond.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara explains that the Sages call betrothal kiddushin because the husband makes her forbidden to everyone like hekdesh, in contrast to the Torah's language of acquisition used in this mishnah.

key_terms.definition: The second stage of marriage, effected through chuppah, when the couple begin to live together and the husband's and wife's mutual financial and marital obligations take effect.
key_terms.on_this_daf: It is distinguished from kiddushin: the ketubah and yichud belong to nisu'in. Tosafot note that the Torah's word for "taking" a woman, from which kiddushin is derived, plainly describes nisu'in.

key_terms.sense: betrothal by giving money or its value
key_terms.definition: One of the three means of betrothal: the man gives the woman money or an object of value before witnesses, stating that she is betrothed to him.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mishnah disputes its minimum value, and the Gemara derives it from Efron's field, which is why the mishnah uses the language of acquisition.

key_terms.definition: One of the three means of betrothal: a single act of intercourse performed before witnesses with the intent to effect kiddushin. For a yevamah, intercourse with the yavam is the only way he acquires her.
key_terms.on_this_daf: It explains the mishnah's choice of the word "ways," since Mishlei calls intercourse a derech. Money and document are also said to serve the purpose of intercourse.

key_terms.definition: The smallest copper coin, one-eighth of an Italian issar. It serves as the halachic minimum of monetary value in many laws.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Beit Hillel set a perutah or its equivalent as the minimum for kiddushei kesef, against Beit Shammai's dinar.

key_terms.definition: A hermeneutic principle by which a law stated in one context is applied to another because the same word appears in both passages.
key_terms.on_this_daf: "Kicha–kicha" links "ki yikach ish isha" to Avraham's purchase of Efron's field, teaching that a woman is betrothed with money. Tosafot question why the analogy is needed and note its imperfection.

key_terms.sense: widow bound to her late husband's brother
key_terms.definition: A widow whose husband died childless, who is bound to his brother (the yavam) for levirate marriage. The bond ends through levirate union or through chalitzah.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mishnah states that the yavam acquires her only through intercourse, and that she goes free through chalitzah or the yavam's death.

key_terms.sense: man impure through abnormal genital discharge
key_terms.definition: A man who has a gonorrhea-like discharge (zivah) and becomes a source of impurity. A discharge caused by an external factor does not render him a zav, so he is examined for such causes.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mishnah "one examines a zav in seven ways" is contrasted with this mishnah's feminine wording and its use of "ways." The Gemara explains that excessive eating and drinking are ways that lead to zivah.
